name: Alethia Stratigraphic Materiality & Geospatial Truth
description: Derived from the Greek 'Alētheia' (unconcealed truth) and terrestrial geology. Eliminates artificial surface gloss in favor of honest mineral textures (obsidian, basalt, raw terra-cotta), stratigraphic elevation cross-sections, and topographic scroll contouring.
designPhilosophy: True permanence is geological. By treating digital space as stratigraphic layers rather than synthetic screens, designs ground themselves in raw, unvarnished reality. Typography mirrors carved stone inscriptions, color palettes derive from earth pigments, and navigation mimics geological elevation cross-sections.
appropriateUseCases: Environmental research and planetary climate showcases
High-end architectural monographs and sustainable design studios
Geological, luxury mineral, and ceramic atelier websites
implementationApproach: 1. Terrestrial Mineral Palette: Basalt Charcoal (#0B0C0E), Raw Slate (#16181D), Ochre Mineral Accent (#C28E52), and Sandstone White (#F5F2EB). 2. Stratigraphic Layer Transitions: Layered depth reveals where sections overlap like geological strata using subtle mask-image linear gradients. 3. Topographical Contour Vectors: SVG elevation curves with scroll-scrubbed stroke-dashoffset.
performanceConsiderations: Vector contour paths simplified to fewer than 50 anchor points each to maintain zero GPU rasterization overhead.
accessibilityRequirements: Text contrast ratio exceeding 12:1 against raw slate and basalt backgrounds. Full screen reader landmark hierarchy.
